NDT training in Jacksonville: how it works for Jacksonville employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training for Jacksonville employers and technicians, either live online or onsite at your own shop, hangar or yard in Northeast Florida. We provide the classroom training; your employer's written practice governs on-the-job experience, examinations and certification, with an ASNT Level III administering the exams. Methods include UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET for Level I and II, plus Level III preparation.

Jacksonville's NDT market is shaped by the sea and the military. Naval aviation depot maintenance, surface ship repair, a large deep-water port, two rail headquarters, a municipal utility with coastal generating stations and a network of long-span bridges all generate inspection work. Salt air and humidity accelerate corrosion on everything from bridge steel to fuel tanks, so thickness surveys, weld inspection and surface crack detection keep technicians busy all year. Many of those jobs also carry Navy or aerospace specifications on top of normal commercial codes, which makes a technician's training record and certification file especially important.

Atlantis has no physical training centre in Jacksonville. Instead, we train your people where they work: live-virtual classrooms for theory and onsite sessions at your facility for hands-on practice and practical examinations, all under ASNT Level III oversight. That suits a ship repair subcontractor on the St. Johns River, an aviation MRO supplier near Cecil Airport, or a fabrication shop on the Northside equally well.

Request a Jacksonville training quote with your methods, levels and headcount.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Jacksonville

Each course follows the ASNT SNT-TC-1A framework and the topical outlines of ANSI/ASNT CP-105. Level I and II courses cover principles, equipment, calibration, technique, interpretation against codes and reporting. Level III preparation covers method depth plus the basic examination. The table maps each method to Jacksonville work.

MethodLevelsWhat Jacksonville employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, III prepHull and structure thickness gauging during ship repair, weld inspection on ship and bridge steel, corrosion surveys on port and utility tanks and pipingLevel I: employer entry requirements. Level II: Level I plus documented experience
Phased Array UT (PAUT)I, IIWeld examination on ship structure and piping, corrosion mapping on tanks and pressure equipment, component inspection in aviation maintenanceConventional UT Level II strongly recommended
Time-of-Flight Diffraction (TOFD)I, IIFlaw sizing on thick welds in pressure equipment and heavy fabricationConventional UT Level II strongly recommended
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, II, III prepPiping and pressure-boundary welds on ships, pressure vessels and pipelines, casting evaluationState radiation safety training and certification required before handling sources
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, II, III prepWeld inspection on ship and bridge steel, rail component inspection, crack detection on steel aircraft and landing-gear parts under the applicable technical dataEmployer entry requirements
Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)I, II, III prepAluminium and non-ferrous aircraft components, stainless and copper-nickel piping welds, castingsEmployer entry requirements
Visual Testing (VT)I, II, III prepWeld visual inspection on ship repair and structural jobs, bridge inspection, pre-repair and post-repair checksEmployer entry requirements
Eddy Current Testing (ET)I, IICrack detection around fastener holes and on aircraft structure, heat exchanger and condenser tubing at generating stations, conductivity checksEmployer entry requirements

For Jacksonville technicians aiming at aviation maintenance, PT, ET and MT are usually the core. For ship repair, VT, MT, UT and RT are the priorities. If you are unsure which route fits a particular contract, book a Level III consultation.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Jacksonville, step by step

Florida does not issue an NDT licence, and ASNT does not issue Level I or II certificates under SNT-TC-1A. The employer certifies. The path for a Jacksonville technician is:

  1. Employer written practice. Your employer documents how it trains, examines and certifies NDT personnel. Without one, nobody can be certified. See written practice development.
  2. Classroom training. You complete the formal training hours your written practice requires. Atlantis delivers these online or onsite. For recommended hours by method and level, use the training requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience. You build documented experience under qualified supervision, for example in a ship repair yard or hangar. The matrix shows recommended minimums; your employer may set more.
  4. General examination on method principles.
  5. Specific examination on your employer's equipment, procedures and specifications, which in Jacksonville often includes Navy or customer technical requirements.
  6. Practical examination on real specimens with real discontinuities, graded by a Level III or designated examiner.
  7. Vision examination, near-vision acuity and colour contrast, at least annually.
  8. Certification by your employer once the Level III has reviewed the record.
  9. Recertification at the interval your written practice sets.

Read more on SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Jacksonville crews

Jacksonville employers operate on tight availability windows. A ship in for a repair availability has a fixed schedule, aviation depot work runs to production targets, and utility outages are planned months ahead. Taking a crew offline to attend a fixed out-of-town course is often the hardest part of training. Atlantis offers:

  • Live online classroom for the theory component of every method and for Level III preparation. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your facility in Jacksonville or the surrounding region, under ASNT Level III oversight, using your equipment and specimens and aligned with your procedures.
  • Blended, with theory online in shorter sessions that fit around shifts and practicals onsite when the crew is available.

We plan around your availability windows, shutdowns and hurricane season disruptions. Ask about onsite training for your Jacksonville crew; cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Jacksonville

Naval aviation maintenance

NAS Jacksonville hosts Fleet Readiness Center Southeast, a major Navy depot for aircraft, engine and component maintenance, and the base is home to maritime patrol aviation. Depot and supplier work relies heavily on PT, MT, ET and UT applied to technical manuals and Navy/aerospace specifications. Cecil Airport and the Cecil Commerce Center on the west side host further aviation maintenance and aerospace tenants. Military aviation programmes generally require NDT personnel qualification to NAS 410 or their own technical requirements; some employers accept SNT-TC-1A for commercial work and use NAS 410 for military contracts. Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A-based, and we are clear about that so employers can decide how it fits their programme.

Ship repair and naval surface fleet

Naval Station Mayport is the Navy's East Coast surface ship homeport in Florida, and private ship repair yards and subcontractors along the St. Johns River support availabilities for Navy and commercial vessels. Navy ship repair NDT is governed by NAVSEA technical publications, notably the requirements for NDT personnel qualification and inspection acceptance in NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 and MIL-STD-2035. These are context: employers working under them set their own qualification rules, and SNT-TC-1A-based training is often the foundation technicians build on. Naval Submarine Base Kings Bay, just across the Georgia line, adds further demand in the region.

Port, terminals and logistics

JAXPORT's marine terminals, Blount Island and the fuel and bulk terminals along the river create steady work on cranes, dock structures, storage tanks and transfer piping. Coastal corrosion makes UT thickness surveys and VT on structures routine, and tank inspection work draws on API 653-based programmes run by owner inspectors (Atlantis does not provide API 653 training, but our UT, MT, PT and VT courses cover the NDT those inspections rely on).

Rail

Jacksonville is the headquarters city for CSX Transportation and the Florida East Coast Railway. Rail work generates MT, UT and VT on wheels, axles, couplers, rail welds and bridges, often under Association of American Railroads and Federal Railroad Administration requirements.

Power generation and utilities

JEA's generating stations and the region's utilities need ET on condenser and heat exchanger tubing, UT on piping and boiler components, and MT and PT on rotating equipment during planned outages.

Bridges and structural steel

Jacksonville's identity is tied to its St. Johns River bridges, several of them long-span steel structures exposed to a marine environment. Bridge fabrication and repair follow AWS D1.5, with UT and MT on critical welds and VT throughout. FDOT and its consultants run ongoing inspection programmes, and commercial structural fabricators work to AWS D1.1.

Radiography licensing in Florida

Florida is an NRC Agreement State, and industrial radiography is licensed and inspected by the Florida Department of Health's radiation control programme. Radiographers must meet state requirements for radiation safety training, certification (for example through ASNT's industrial radiography radiation safety personnel programme or another recognised certification), on-the-job training, and dosimetry, and must work under a licensed company with a radiation safety officer. Atlantis RT courses teach the NDT method; the state-required radiation safety component is separate and runs through your employer's licensed programme. Always confirm current rules with the Florida Department of Health before handling a source.

What Jacksonville employers typically ask for

  • SNT-TC-1A Level II certification with a complete, auditable file.
  • For Navy ship repair, familiarity with NAVSEA requirements and a willingness to be qualified under the employer's Navy-compliant programme.
  • For aviation work, PT, ET and MT depth, attention to technical data, and awareness that military work may require NAS 410.
  • Base access requirements such as security screening, handled by the employer.
  • Some employers also ask for welding inspector credentials; Atlantis does not deliver those courses.

Level III services and written practices for Jacksonville NDT companies

Small ship repair subcontractors, fabrication shops and aviation suppliers in Jacksonville often need a Level III without the overhead of a full-time hire. Under SNT-TC-1A an employer can designate an outside Level III, and Atlantis provides that service:

  • Written practice development tailored to your methods and customers. See written practice development.
  • Procedure development referencing the codes and specifications you work to.
  • Examinations: general, specific and practical, prepared and graded by a Level III.
  • Audit support for customer, prime contractor and quality-system audits.
  • Corporate training plans: see corporate NDT training.

Start with SNT-TC-1A training and certification, then book a Level III consultation for your Jacksonville company.

Practise before the practical exam

Atlantis's Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 NDT methods across five environments: NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site and storage tank. For Jacksonville trainees, the aircraft hangar and welding workshop scenarios map closely to aviation depot and ship repair work, and the storage tank scenario fits terminal inspection.

The simulator is practice only. It does not replace hands-on training or the practical examination on real specimens required by your written practice.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He oversees course content, examinations and employer certification support for Jacksonville clients, online and onsite. Level III candidates can review ASNT Level III training.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Jacksonville

How do I get NDT certified in Jacksonville?

Under SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you after you complete classroom training, documented on-the-job experience, general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, and a vision test. Atlantis provides the training and can act as your employer's outside Level III.

Can I take NDT training online in Florida?

Yes. Theory for all methods and Level III preparation are available as live online classes. Practical training and exams are completed on real equipment and specimens, which we deliver onsite. See online NDT training.

Is there an Atlantis NDT school in Jacksonville?

No. Atlantis has no physical training centre in Jacksonville. We train online and onsite at your company's facility.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum classroom hours and experience for each level, listed in our training requirements matrix. The experience requirement usually determines the overall timeline.

Do I need a license for radiography in Florida?

Florida is an Agreement State, so radiography companies are licensed by the Florida Department of Health, and radiographers must meet state radiation safety training and certification requirements before working with sources. This is separate from NDT certification in RT.

What does NDT training cost in Jacksonville?

Pricing is on request and depends on method, level, group size and delivery format. Request a Jacksonville training quote; we respond within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Jacksonville employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the standard framework for most US commercial NDT work, including fabrication, utilities, rail and many contractors. Navy and military aviation work may impose additional or different qualification requirements, such as NAVSEA or NAS 410, which the employer manages.

Do you offer NAS 410 or NAVSEA-specific training?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based. Many technicians use SNT-TC-1A training as a foundation before being qualified under an employer's NAS 410 or NAVSEA programme, but we do not certify to those schemes.

Which NDT method is most useful in Jacksonville?

For aviation maintenance, PT and ET. For ship repair and structural work, VT, MT and UT. RT and PAUT add value for piping and pressure work.

Can you train our crew onsite at our Jacksonville facility?

Yes, under ASNT Level III oversight and scheduled around your availabilities and outages. See corporate NDT training.

Does my company need a written practice?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A requires an employer written practice before anyone is certified. We can build one for you through written practice development.

How should I prepare for the UT Level II exam?

Work through UT Level 2 practice questions for the written exams and use the Practical NDT simulator to rehearse scan technique before your real practical.
